subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should shared-workspace memory-core dreaming be agent-isolated by default, or is workspace-level pooling an accepted behavior that should be opt-in/documented?
rationale: The code fix is straightforward enough to locate, but the permanent boundary affects privacy, existing shared-workspace operators, derived memory artifacts, and the public multi-agent isolation contract.

options.title: Enforce Agent Isolation By Default
options.body: Treat cross-agent dreaming ingestion as a security/session-state bug and require the fix to preserve one agent boundary through ingestion, recall, narrative, and promotion, with migration or repair for pooled artifacts.

options.title: Accept Explicit Allowlist Control
options.body: Land the focused allowlist/config path as an operator-controlled mitigation while tracking automatic shared-workspace isolation separately.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling As Expected
options.body: Close the bug direction only if maintainers intentionally decide shared workspace means shared dreaming memory and update multi-agent docs to say so clearly.

recommendation.title: Enforce Agent Isolation By Default
recommendation.body: Treat cross-agent dreaming ingestion as a security/session-state bug and require the fix to preserve one agent boundary through ingestion, recall, narrative, and promotion, with migration or repair for pooled artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the issue, already narrowed the behavior question in comments, and have recent adjacent memory-core dreaming history.
